expectations.text: Recommends splitting the class by responsibility (does NOT endorse keeping all 4 concerns in one file)
expectations.evidence: 'Short answer: no, I'd split it'; 'Split along the four seams' into authTokenService.ts, userRepository.ts, userNotifier.ts, userAnalytics.ts plus optional thin userService.ts orchestrator.

expectations.text: Identifies the seams (auth / persistence / email / analytics) as genuinely independent and isolatable
expectations.evidence: 'four independent capabilities that happen to share the word user'; details different dependencies, reasons to change, and testing modes per concern; 'the seams already exist, you're just making them explicit.'

expectations.text: Cites the ~300-line ceiling AND/OR multiple-unrelated-concerns as the reason, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'splitting is justified by genuine independence, not a line count'; frames it as a textbook single-responsibility violation across four distinct external dependencies rather than blind size.

expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'keep everything in one place for the agent' rationale as misapplied to a god object
expectations.evidence: 'Why one file isn't actually helping the AI'; 'A well-named file is a much stronger signal to an AI agent than physical proximity'; 'solving a navigation problem you don't have at the cost of focus you do need.'
